newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares little changed, seen quiet.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares little changed, seen quiet.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were little changed in early trade on Monday and traders said they would be range-bound during the day on low demand due to continuing investor interest in less liquid shares.
The Russian Trading System of 22 shares opened slightly up on Monday at 355.82 after 355.64 on Friday.
But traders said slack demand from both Russian and foreign investors would keep the market fairly quiet over the week.

"The wave of the May holidays lifted "blue chips". After that there is traditionally always a wave of demand which raises second-tier shares," said United City Bank senior trader Samit Yakovlev, seeing leading shares easing on the changeover.

"I think the general background is positive -- good political and general economic news, so there's no call to expect a major fall, although you can't expect a rise either in this kind of absence of client interest."
National utlity UES EESR.RTS slipped to $0.3143 at 1320 GMT from $0.3170 on Friday, while Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS eased to $0.8570 from $0.8625.
Traders said low volumes were softening the effect of a decision by Surgutneftegaz shareholders over the weekend to limit individual stakes to one percent of voting shares.

"Obviously client activity is very low today and so a reaction as such has not yet occurred, but I can't say the percentage limit on voting in Surgut is positive news," said Ilya Galtsov, head of trading at Trinfiko.
Galtsov said domestic demand was slipping as Treasury bill yields firmed from recent low levels.
He said less liquid shares in regional telecoms, which trade on the second tier of the RTS, were still attracting investors, along with some metallurgical and chemical plants.
"The last wave of demand for those securities hasn't finished yet, although it might be close to over," Galtsov said.
"Demand for second tier stocks has become more selective: people are choosign securities based on fundamental indicators."
